overview: Poldhu Cove is a sandy beach on the west coast of the Lizard, just north of Mullion, between Mullion and Gunwalloe. With lifeguards in season and a car park, toilets and a café close by, it’s a reliable family beach.

The clifftop above has a place in history: on 12 December 1901, a radio signal sent from Marconi’s station at Poldhu was received across the Atlantic in Newfoundland, the first transatlantic radio message, and the forerunner of radio, television and the internet.

expect.title: The beach
expect.text: A medium-sized sandy cove between headlands.

expect.title: Marconi history
expect.text: Up on the clifftop there’s a memorial pillar put up by the Marconi Company in 1937, and the Marconi Centre nearby tells the story of the wireless station.

expect.title: Coast path
expect.text: Walk south along the cliffs to Polurrian and Mullion Cove, or north to Church Cove at Gunwalloe.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: In the north of Mullion parish, about 2 km from Mullion village, on the Mount’s Bay side of the Lizard.

week.text: A dependable family beach day on the Lizard, with history thrown in. Combine it with a coast path walk to Mullion Cove, or a look at Church Cove at Gunwalloe just to the north.

pairWith.why: a pretty cove with a church by the beach at Gunwalloe
the story of the 1901 radio message
a little harbour along the coast path

tips: Walk up to the clifftop for the Marconi monument and big views over Mount’s Bay.
